messages.subject: c-hat, QAIC, and model selection
parts:
Hello, 

I've been reading through threads related to this question, but I think this question will address new aspects of the subject.  

I'm modeling single-species, single-season occupancy for 15 songbirds.  The process I follow is as follows: 

1. run the global model.
2. use mb.gof.test to calculate c-hat.
3. run 10 a priori models of detection probability (occupancy constant).
4. rank detection models with QAIC with c-hat specified (c-hat ranged from 1-3.5 for 12 species to 5.1 - 10 for 3 species). 

Before continuing, I have a few question about these steps.   I assumed that since the mb.gof.test is looking at detection history it is appropriate to rank detection models with QAIC by c-hat (when c-hat >1).  On more than 1 occasion, the null model has been the QAIC best detection model.  Is it appropriate to use intercept-only (~1) for detection moving forward to occupancy? 

5. run all subsequent occupancy models with detection covariates from the top detection model.
6. run 10 a priori models of occupancy.
7. rank with QAIC with c-hat specified (when c-hat > 1). 

When running the global model in order to calculate c-hat, should this be the full model of detection AND occupancy (eg. y ~ X1 + X2 + X3 ~ X4 + X5 + X6), or just the global model of detection?

When c-hat is greater than 4, the models can not be ranked with QAIC because the cut-off is 4; should this species be eliminated from analysis as ability to make inferences will be weak to non-existent any how, or should one  write a custom function to rank by QAIC while allowing c-hat to be > 4 (one of these species was of primary interest [c-hat = 5.1])?

The survey design included 4 visits to 300 points (1 visit was at the very end of the breeding season), and I found that for 2 species where c-hat is > 4, I can reduce this issue by removing the 4th round of surveys and treating it as a 3 visit design.  Is this something that might be frowned upon?

Finally, after ranking occupancy models with QAIC, there's 1 species where the null-model is highly ranked, and more complex models have borderline informative parameters (95% CI crosses zero, but 85% CI does not after inflating SE*sqrt(c-hat)).  Is this a model/species that should maybe be removed from the discussion?

I hope this question is not redundant, and I appreciate any insight the group may have 

Thanks
-Dan
